title: Maximum Product of Three Elements After One Replacement
summary: Given an integer array, replace exactly one element with any integer in the range [-100000, 100000] to maximize the product of any three distinct elements in the array.
statement: Given an integer array, replace exactly one element with any integer in the range [-100000, 100000] to maximize the product of any three distinct elements in the array. Return the maximum product.
constraints: nums contains three to 100,000 integers in [-100000,100000].
Replace exactly one element by any integer in that same range.
After replacement, maximize the product of values at three distinct indices.
hints: The replacement appears in an optimal triple and its best value is one of the allowed range endpoints.
After sorting, only the two smallest, two largest, or one smallest plus one largest retained values can maximize the paired factor.
Evaluate those three pair patterns with replacement +100000 or -100000 as appropriate.
For a linear product in the replacement, an endpoint is optimal; the extreme-pair property covers the maximum product of any two retained values or its negation.
editorial: For a linear product in the replacement, an endpoint is optimal; the extreme-pair property covers the maximum product of any two retained values or its negation.

tests.explanation: Two large-magnitude negatives with a replacement of 100000 give 1,200,000.
